            int backtrace_format (char * buf, size_t buf_size, const char *
              label, const backtrace_t * bt, int skip_frames, int
              max_frames, backtrace_frame_filter_t filter)
          

          

            Format backtrace to buffer (plain ASCII, no colors). Formats a
            backtrace into a plain ASCII buffer without ANSI color codes. This
            is the safe choice for:
          

          
    
            
  • Generating log file content
    • 
            
  • Embedding in error messages or email alerts
    • 
            
  • Storing in databases or structured logs
    • 
            
  • Sending over network protocols
    • 
          

          

            The buffer must not be freed before use - the returned count is the
            number of bytes written. The buffer is null-terminated if space
            permits.
          

          

        

        

          

            Output Example
          

          
char buffer[2048];
backtrace_t bt;
backtrace_capture_and_symbolize(&bt);
int written = backtrace_format(buffer, sizeof(buffer),


                               "Crash", &bt, 0, 10, NULL);
if (written > 0) {


    // Safe to use with logging system


    log_error("Program crashed:\n%s", buffer);


    // Safe to include in structured fields


    json_add_string(crash_report, "backtrace", buffer);
}

          
Parameters

          

            buf Output buffer (will be null-terminated if space permits)
            

            buf_size Size of output buffer in bytes (must be at least 1)
            

            label Header label (e.g., "Crash",
            "Assertion")
            

            bt Backtrace to format (must not be NULL, must be symbolized)
            

            skip_frames Number of frames to skip from start (0 = all)
            

            max_frames Maximum frames to include (0 = unlimited)
            

            filter Optional filter callback (NULL = no filtering)
          

          
Returns

          

            Number of bytes written (not including null terminator), or -1 on
            error If buffer is too small, returns the bytes that would be
            written if space allowed
          

          
Note

          

            Buffer is always null-terminated on success (output < buf_size)
            

            

              This is the preferred output method for integration with
              structured logging
            

            

            

              No ANSI color codes are included, making output safe for any
              destination
            

          

          
See also

          

            backtrace_print() for dual (colored terminal + plain log
            file) output

            void backtrace_print (log_level_t level, const char *
              label, const backtrace_t * bt, int skip_frames, int
              max_frames, backtrace_frame_filter_t filter)
          

          

            Print backtrace with dual output: colored stderr + plain log file.
            Intelligently formats and routes backtraces to multiple
            destinations:
          

          
    
            
  • 
              stderr: Colored output with semantic highlighting (for
              interactive debugging)
            
    • 
            
  • 
              log file (if logging): Plain ASCII without ANSI codes (for
              file parsing)
            
    • 
          

          

            This dual-output design ensures readable terminal output during
            development while keeping log files clean and searchable in
            production.
          

          

        

        

          

            Output Format
          

          
Terminal output example:

          

          
=== Backtrace: Error ===
[0] 0x7f1234567890 in main() [src/main.c:42]
[1] 0x7f1234567800 in process_request() [src/network.c:128]
[2] 0x7f1234567700 in send_data() [src/io.c:67]


          
Log file (same content, no colors):

          

          
=== Backtrace: Error ===
[0] 0x7f1234567890 in main() [src/main.c:42]
...


          
Parameters

          

            level Log severity for the entire backtrace entry
            

            label Header label (e.g., "Backtrace", "Leak
            trace", "Assertion failure")
            

            bt Backtrace to print (must not be NULL, must be symbolized
            via backtrace_capture_and_symbolize)
            

            skip_frames Number of frames to skip from start (0 = include
            all, 1 = skip first frame, etc.)
            

            max_frames Maximum frames to print (0 = unlimited, 5 = first
            5 frames only)
            

            filter Optional callback to selectively skip frames (e.g.,
            filter internal frames) Return true to skip frame, false to include.
            NULL = no filtering.
          

          
Note

          

            Backtrace must be symbolized. Unsymbolized (raw hex) traces are less
            useful.
            

            

              Frame filtering is useful to focus on application code, excluding:
            

            
    
              
  • lib/platform internal calls
    • 
              
  • lib/log infrastructure
    • 
              
  • Exception handling wrappers
    • 
            

          

          
See also

          

            backtrace_format() for buffer-based output (safe for log
            system)
